The United States is now run by someone whose critics and victims routinely
dub an American "psycho," a man who revels in the pain and suffering of his
enemies and his prey. Indeed, many of his allies, and his past and present
colleagues, would describe him using precisely the same word.

We are, of course, talking about Stephen Miller, not his boss, Donald Trump.

Miller, who serves as Trump's top policy architect and one of the president's
most committed loyalists, doesn't care about human life the way you or I do,
former and current Trump administration officials who've worked with him tell
**Zeteo**. Several of these sources actually quite like Miller. Still, the
degree to which Miller does not care about - or at least tolerates - the loss
of human lives in the pursuit of his and President Trump's policy vision has
unnerved, or disturbed, some of his Republican colleagues, multiple Trump
advisers and U.S. government officials recount.

Some of his associates in and close to the administration even accuse him of
intentionally trying to push major U.S. cities to riot, to create a pretext
for Trump to invoke the Insurrection Act, an early 19th-century law, so that
he could send thousands of active-duty and National Guard troops to fully
occupy those urban areas. One source directly familiar with Miller's private
deliberations tells **Zeteo** : "Stephen wanted to provoke a very strong
response, so that the president would deploy troops."

It has been just under two years since Trump won the presidency for the second
time, and the scale of democratic backsliding, rampant corruption, and sheer
violence unleashed on this continent and others is remarkably difficult to
tabulate. The administration has normalized putting troops in the streets;
deploying masked, violent immigration agents to kidnap and intimidate and kill
people; punishing immigrants, including many with a legal right to be here, by
shipping them to dangerous countries, including places where they have no
ties, simply to be cruel; murdering supposed drug smugglers with regularity in
international waters; tearing apart the core constitutional right to due
process at every opportunity, so that people can't challenge the government's
claims against them before they are removed or killed; politicizing every
lever of the government so that it targets their enemies, and only their
enemies, as part of a swarming attack on Democrats and the left and liberal
nonprofit and political infrastructure; actively ignoring the First Amendment;
spewing the most blatant kinds of racism from the White House, including at
Somali Americans and Haitians; plotting in broad daylight to rig elections and
subvert the American democratic order; and so, so much more.

On Trump's behalf, Miller has overseen, or orchestrated, all of it. He has led
Trump's deportation operations and the president's efforts to target and
selectively prosecute his enemies at an intensely granular level. That
includes overseeing what a Trump adviser described to **Zeteo** as the
administration's "Must Deport list." When Miller has discussed behind closed
doors the administration's deportations to third-countries (where the
immigrants have no ties), he has explicitly said that it is better to strike
those agreements with nations with lousy human rights records - in part
because those regimes often do what they're told by the United States, sources
who've been in the room with him say.

It is impossible to come to any other conclusion: At almost every single
meaningful turn of the second Trump era, the president's lead policy author
has sought to make the government's crackdowns more painful, and less humane,
for its countless dragnet victims and their families.

Let that be his, and his boss's, legacy - and perhaps their undoing.
